speaker: dorcas_ansell
text: Look at him. A jaw like a quince.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: It is a tooth, Mistress. It has a side, and the side is the left.

speaker: dorcas_ansell
text: There is Master Yaxley in Bishopsgate Street will have it out for a shilling, as I am a Christian woman.

speaker: dorcas_ansell
text: A man who can walk a hundred miles for a barn can walk forty yards for a tooth.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: After Thursday, Mistress.

speaker: dorcas_ansell
text: What is Thursday?

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: The king.

speaker: dorcas_ansell
text: The one put down by his cousin.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: That one.

speaker: dorcas_ansell
text: Then you will speak his uncle's dying with a face like a pudding, and it will serve you both right.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: He is past caring how the face looks. I am not. The speech is already in the mouth, and I will not have the mouth emptied before it has been said.

speaker: gillis_verbeke
text: In Ghent they tie a thread to the tooth and the other end to a door. A friend who does not love you too much shuts the door.

speaker: alse_pinder
text: I cannot hear of the door, sir. I will be in the kitchen.

speaker: dorcas_ansell
text: Let her go. She has a soft heart and a full tray, and the tray is the useful half.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: Saturday was thirty-four shillings, the best since Whitsun. I would give half of it to chew.

speaker: dorcas_ansell
text: You will give Master Yaxley a shilling, when you give it, and you will keep your player's money for a week in which you can eat. I am not pricing a jaw.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: I am not paying him today. The king has this week. The tooth can wait upon a Thursday, which is more patience than it has shown me.

speaker: gillis_verbeke
text: A door does not wait upon a king. That is why a door is honest. I do not offer you mine. I have not loved you long enough to be the man who shuts it.

speaker: dorcas_ansell
text: Sit. The broth is on the board, and there are sops in it, which is as much mercy as a Sunday gets from me.

speaker: alse_pinder
text: Sops, sir. The crust is in them, so you need not chew the crust. I will not ask about the door again.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: Thank you, Alse. The door can stay as it is. I am not ready to be improved by it.

speaker: alse_pinder
text: Then I am glad I left when I did. The broth is hot on the near side. I will take the bit of crust that would not go soft.

speaker: dorcas_ansell
text: Eat what you can, and write to your wife before the light goes. Thursday's carrier will not wait upon a pudding.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: Six lines. She shall have the margin, and she shall have that I have a tooth. She shall not have the Mayor's letter. There is nothing in that letter she can use.

speaker: dorcas_ansell
text: The letter is yours. The table is mine. The quince stays here until Thursday, and after Thursday you will walk the forty yards or you will hear of it at every meal.

speaker: gillis_verbeke
text: I will say no more about Ghent. The sops do not love you at all, which is a kind of safety, and safety is the most I came downstairs to offer.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: Then I will trust the sops. Half a share would not buy a quieter jaw. A shilling might, and the shilling is not today's.

speaker: alse_pinder
text: Shall I take that crust away now, sir?

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: Take it. I have had the mercy. I do not need the crust to prove it.

speaker: dorcas_ansell
text: Upstairs when you are done. The ink is where you left it. I will not have a letter written over a bowl.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: When the bowl is done. The carrier comes before I am ready for him, and I know that much without a sermon.
